card.name: Punctuation after fatal or serious harm
card.fires_on: The comma, verb or word ending right after a severe-outcome phrase such as "fatal", "life-threatening" or "Embryo-Fetal Toxic" in warning sections. It fires where the sentence is about to name the reaction or the affected patients.

modes.label: Comma after fatal
modes.description: A comma following "fatal" or a similar severity word in a warning list.
modes.example: WARNING Severe liver injury and acute liver failure, in some cases fatal<<,>> have been reported in patients treated with prop

modes.label: Have occurred
modes.description: The verb "occurred" after "life-threatening cases have" or "reactions have".
modes.example: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS • Herpes infections: Life-threatening and fatal cases have<< occurred>> with herpes encephalitis and mening

modes.label: End of Toxicity
modes.description: The final piece of the heading "Embryo-Fetal Toxicity".
modes.example: 5.6 Embryo-Fetal Toxic<<ity>> Based on its mechanism of action and findings
